description: The animation framework and the review checklist from references/polish.md, plus the loading-state rules.

gates.title: No transition: all
gates.rule: Transitions name their properties. transition: all animates whatever happens to change, including layout properties, and costs frames for effects nobody asked for.
gates.fix: Specify: transition: transform 200ms var(--ease-out), opacity 200ms var(--ease-out).

gates.title: Nothing Animates From scale(0)
gates.rule: Entrances start at scale(0.9) or higher with opacity. Nothing in the real world vanishes to a point and reappears from one.
gates.fix: Start from scale(0.95) with opacity: 0.

gates.title: No ease-in On UI
gates.rule: ease-in starts slow, which delays movement at exactly the moment the user is watching. Entering and exiting use ease-out; on-screen movement uses ease-in-out; hover and colour use ease; constant motion uses linear.
gates.fix: Switch to ease-out or the project's custom curve.

gates.title: Custom Easing Curves, Defined As Tokens
gates.rule: The built-in CSS easings are too weak to read as intentional. Define --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), --ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1), and the drawer curve, and reference them.
gates.fix: Add the easing tokens to :root and point every transition at them.

gates.title: No Overshoot Easing On UI State
gates.rule: Bouncy cubic-beziers belong to physical interactions — a dragged sheet, a pulled refresh. On a button, modal, or tooltip they read as a toy.
gates.fix: Replace with the standard ease-out token on UI state changes.

gates.title: UI Motion Stays Under 300ms
gates.rule: Button press 100–160ms; tooltips and small popovers 125–200ms; dropdowns and selects 150–250ms; modals and drawers 200–500ms. Nothing else on the interface exceeds 300ms.
gates.fix: Bring the duration into 150–250ms.

gates.title: Only transform And opacity Animate
gates.rule: width, height, top, left, margin, and padding trigger layout and paint. transform and opacity run on the GPU. Position changes go through transform.
gates.fix: Rewrite the animation onto transform/opacity; use scale or translate instead of size and position.

gates.title: Keyboard-Initiated Actions Do Not Animate
gates.rule: Command palettes, shortcut-driven toggles, and anything a user hits a hundred times a day open with no animation at all. Animation there reads as lag.
gates.fix: Remove the animation from the keyboard path; keep it on the mouse path only if it earns its place.

gates.title: Every Animation Has A Stated Purpose
gates.rule: Spatial consistency, state indication, explanation, feedback, or preventing a jarring change. 'It looks cool' on something seen daily is not a purpose.
gates.fix: Name the purpose per animation, or delete it.

gates.title: Popovers Are Origin-Aware
gates.rule: A popover scales from its trigger, not from its own centre. Radix and Base UI expose the transform-origin variable; use it. Modals are exempt and stay centred.
gates.fix: Set transform-origin to var(--radix-popover-content-transform-origin) or the equivalent.

gates.title: Exit Is Faster Than Enter
gates.rule: Exit runs at roughly 60–70% of the enter duration. Matching them makes dismissal feel like the interface is arguing with the user.
gates.fix: Shorten the exit transition.

gates.title: Lists Stagger, They Do Not Arrive At Once
gates.rule: Grid and list entrances stagger 30–80ms per item. Everything appearing on the same frame reads as a page repaint, not an arrival.
gates.fix: Add a per-index delay of 30–80ms, capped so long lists do not crawl.

gates.title: CSS Transitions For Interruptible UI
gates.rule: Rapidly-triggered elements use transitions, not keyframes — a keyframe animation restarted mid-flight snaps. Predetermined motion goes in CSS (off main thread); dynamic interruptible motion goes in JS.
gates.fix: Convert the keyframe animation on the hot element to a transition.

gates.title: Framer Motion Uses Full Transform Strings
gates.rule: The x, y, and scale shorthands are not hardware accelerated — they run on the main thread and drop frames under load. animate={{ transform: 'translateX(100px)' }} does not.
gates.fix: Use the full transform string.

gates.title: Reduced Motion Has A Real Fallback
gates.rule: Every transform and keyframe has an answer under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce). Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not none — keep opacity and colour transitions that aid comprehension, drop movement.
gates.fix: Add the reduced-motion block; strip transforms, keep fades.

gates.title: Unknown, Empty, And Failed Are Three Different States
gates.rule: Data starts as null (unknown), not [] (empty). The empty state waits until the server has actually answered. A failed request shows a failure, never a skeleton that shimmers forever.
gates.fix: Initialise to null, branch on unknown vs empty vs failed, and give the failure its own message and retry.

gates.title: One Skeleton Primitive, Shaped Like Its Content
gates.rule: A single Skeleton primitive and one Loading composition, reused. Each placeholder matches the real box — chart height, row height — so nothing shifts when it resolves. Per-screen bespoke skeletons are how a codebase ends up with nine.
gates.fix: Extract the shared primitive and match the placeholder box to the real one.

gates.title: Content Animates In When Its Skeleton Resolves
gates.rule: Content does not snap in. It animates once, with the same entrance used for page changes.
gates.fix: Apply the shared entrance to the resolved content, once.

gates.title: Loading Shows After 300ms, Not Before
gates.rule: Work under 300ms shows nothing — a flashed spinner is worse than a brief wait. Past 300ms, show the skeleton. Past a second, show progress.
gates.fix: Delay the loading indicator by 300ms.

gates.title: No Toast For A Visible Success
gates.rule: Toasts are for failures and for effects the user cannot see. Confirming something they are already looking at is noise.
gates.fix: Delete the success toast where the effect is on screen; keep it for background work.

gates.title: Tooltip Delays Differ For Hover And Focus
gates.rule: Hover delays 800–1000ms; focus opens at 0ms. Once one tooltip is open, subsequent ones in the same group skip the delay and the animation.
gates.fix: Split the two delays and add the skip-delay window.

gates.title: Auto-Rotating Content Pauses On Hover And Focus
gates.rule: Carousels, rotating banners, and cycling stats stop when the pointer or keyboard reaches them. WCAG 2.2.2.
gates.fix: Pause on mouseenter and focusin; resume on leave and blur.

gates.title: Navigation Motion Follows Its Own Rules
gates.rule: Nav bars, menus, dropdowns, sidebars, hamburger morphs, and active indicators use the per-element timings, stagger, and easing in references/navigation-menus.md rather than the generic transition.
gates.fix: Read navigation-menus.md and apply the timings for the element in question.

gates.title: Motion Is Interruptible And Never Blocks Input
gates.rule: A tap or gesture cancels an in-flight animation immediately, and the interface stays interactive throughout. An animation the user has to wait out is a modal nobody asked for.
gates.fix: Use transitions or interruptible springs; never gate input on animation completion.

gates.title: At Most Two Elements Animate Per View
gates.rule: One or two key elements carry the motion in any given view. Everything moving at once is a screensaver.
gates.fix: Pick the two that matter and still the rest.
